title: Onion Purple Blotch and Thrips Management and Storage Guidelines
source_name: ICAR - Directorate of Onion and Garlic Research (DOGR) Rajgurunagar & MPKV Rahuri
summary: Purple blotch (Alternaria porri) causes sunken purplish lesions on onion leaves and flower stalks, exacerbated by thrips feeding injury.
content: Symptoms of Thrips (Thrips tabaci): Silver-white curling flecks along leaf bases and folded leaves, distorted tips. Symptoms of Purple Blotch: Small water-soaked lesions turning purple-brown with yellow halo, blighted leaf tops leading to reduced bulb size. Actions: 1) Blue sticky traps @ 20 traps/acre installed just above onion foliage to monitor thrips. 2) Sprinkler irrigation reduces thrips population naturally compared to flood or furrow. 3) Organic control: Spray Verticillium lecanii or Beauveria bassiana @ 5 g/L with sticker/spreader in evening. 4) Chemical spray for thrips & blotch complex: Fipronil 5% SC @ 1.5 ml/L OR Spinetoram 11.7% SC @ 0.8 ml/L combined with Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5 g/L or Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1 ml/L. Always add non-ionic wetting agent (sticker) 0.5 ml/L because onion leaves have waxy cuticle. Harvesting & Storage: Withhold irrigation 10-15 days prior to harvest. Cure bulbs in shade with 2-3 cm neck for 7 days before cold/ventilated godown storage.
